column5: Canonical Find My tag reference: adv byte layout, nRF51/ESP32/Linux firmware, macOS app. Read the firmware, do NOT copy AGPL code into a permissive firmware.
The maintained end-to-end stack (key gen, docker endpoint, Android/web UI, ESP32+nRF5x firmware). Our bring-up path if we go the OpenHaystack route.
Best-maintained (v0.10.1, 2026-06) report fetch/decrypt library; MIT so usable in our tools/. Also decodes status bytes of scanned tags.
Firmware ports for the cheap silicon we care about: Lenze ST17H66 ($1 Ali tags), Telink TLSR825X, WCH CH592, plus key generation. Licence unclear - treat as read-only reference.
Origin of every low-power nRF5x Find My firmware; SoftDevice-based, MIT, so we can actually derive from it.
The maintained acalatrava descendant: nRF52810/nRF52832 targets, MAX_KEYS=500 rolling keys, TX-power stepping, DC/DC build variants. Closest match to our nRF52 BOM.
nRF51 firmware with hourly key rotation and a working status-byte side channel (battery bits + event counter) - the pattern for getting sensor state out over Find My.
Zephyr module form of the tag; MIT and RTOS-portable, the cleanest base if halo firmware targets Zephyr/NCS.
Pre-generated key list + one-beacon-per-key firmware. Shows exactly how key rotation is implemented on ESP32 and what anti-stalking evasion looks like (so we can refuse to do it).
Data-over-Find-My modem. Reference for using the key space as a low-rate uplink for sensor telemetry.
Android/iOS detector. Test harness: if AirGuard flags a halo correctly, our DULT behaviour is right.
Required Apple-ID auth shim for Mac-free report fetching. Needed to run our own endpoint.
Reverse-engineered Tile BLE protocol; the only open client for a non-Apple/non-Google finding network.
Google's own Fast Pair/Find Hub reference code; the network-agnostic second radio path for halo.

Only open round coin-cell nRF52832 tag with KiCad sources, a routed NFC-A coil and a routed LIS2DH12; 8 production revisions. Layout donor. Share-alike -- decide copy-vs-redraw before touching copper.
The only open KiCad Apple-Find-My tag with a sounder. Reference implementation for the E73 module + piezo + battery-holder approach; reciprocal licence, safe to build on.

Best Find My + Google FMDN firmware base (Zephyr, nRF52805/810/832/833, nRF54L15, BLE-reconfigurable, active 2026-04). hardware/ also has a complete KiCad + gerber Qi-charging beacon we can lift the BQ25121A block from.
Permissively licensed complete CR2032 nRF52 beacon: schematic + PCB + gerbers + STEP housing. Safest design to copy outright from.

Nordic's own nRF52832 QFAA / QFAA-DCDC / QFAA-NFC reference layouts (Eagle + PDF). Source of the matching network and antenna for a bare-chip halo variant. NOTE Nordic says only the Altium versions are verified.
KiCad symbols + footprints for modern Nordic parts, packaged with reference-design blocks -- the closest existing model for halo-core as a reusable KiCad block.
Nordic QFAA-DCDC reference converted to KiCad via altium2kicad and cleaned up. Shortcut to a KiCad-native nRF52 RF section; three conversions deep, re-verify against Nordic's Altium PDF.
Parametric NFC coil generator that emits KiCad modules -- needed for the AirTag-parity NFC-A antenna on a 30 mm disc.
KiCad inverted-F 2.4 GHz antenna footprints; starting point for the bare-chip halo antenna and the documented keep-out.
Puck.js round nRF52832 CR2032 puck schematics plus an Eagle part library for the Raytac MDBT42Q module -- prior art for "RF as a reusable part".

Only maintained Zephyr driver for DW3000; carries the official Qorvo dwt_uwb_driver source plus the DW3000 User Manual and the DWS3000 shield schematics we need as an open RF front-end reference. Read the Qorvo field-of-use clause before linking it into halo firmware.
Clean, small TWR implementation on top of the Qorvo driver, with IRQ handling for Zephyr/ESP-IDF/nRF-SDK. The reference for how halo-uwb should do SS-TWR without pulling in Qorvo example bloat.

The most mature open UWB anchor/tag firmware (active 2026-09), with TWR, TDoA2 and TDoA3 in one codebase, from a company that also opens its hardware. Reference for protocol structure and for how a fleet schedules air time.

Contains the reference Channel Sounding RAS initiator/reflector samples and the sample.yaml that proves nRF54L05/L10 are CS build targets. Vendor only the channel_sounding sample tree, not the whole SDK.
The closest existing board to halo-uwb: a BLE SoC plus DW3000 on one PCB, with schematics. Useful as a layout sanity check even though the licence is unstated (do not copy artwork).

Board schematic PDF plus the NConcepts DW3000 Arduino library and multi-tag/multi-anchor examples; the most widely reproduced hobby DW3000 platform, so it is what any halo-uwb bring-up will be compared against.
The canonical open DW1000 driver (574 stars) and the ancestor of most open UWB ranging code; permissively licensed, so it is the one UWB codebase whose licence never blocks us.
MIT-licensed cooperative relative localization from pairwise UWB ranges - the closest working code to the halo fleet self-location problem, and the starting point for the Twinton-side solver.

Solves anchor positions from ranges alone - exactly the anchor-free survey halo needs. Archived and self-declared unverified, so vendor it as a reference algorithm (Batstone/LTH) rather than as a dependency.
Curated index of every Channel Sounding vendor doc, chip and dev board; cheap to keep locally as the entry point for the CS literature that lane H only sampled.
MIT AT-command layer for setting up CS ranging sessions and extracting raw IQ data - a ready-made bench harness for the orientation/multipath experiment recommended in research/08 section 14.

column4: ~25 MB (Documents/ holds two 6.7 MB Apollo3 datasheets + a 5.4 MB STEP)
column5: The only open-source-hardware CERTIFIED castellated module with full design files. The exact artefact halo-core wants to be: 4-layer module, 2-layer host, 15.5x10.5 mm, FCC ID 2ASW8-ART3MIS, ships STEP+STL of the module for host 3D views. Copy its repo layout, its integration-guide structure and its pad-numbering discipline.
The "all the pins" carrier board for the Artemis module — the worked example of a host board that breaks out every module pad. Reference for the halo-core breakout/dev host.

column3: stated only as "see the LICENSE file" — CHECK BEFORE USE
column4: ~100 MB (many boards + Fritzing parts + enclosure boxes)
column5: Puck.js is a shipping coin-cell nRF52832 product built on the SAME Raytac MDBT42Q this lane recommends, and the repo carries an Eagle library for the MDBT42 part plus an MDBT42Q breakout board. Closest existing prior art for halo-core v1's construction.

column3: CC BY-SA 4.0 (README, Lauri Jamsa / Ruuvi Innovations)
column5: The best-documented open coin-cell nRF52832 tag: real KiCad sources, a working NFC-A tag antenna already laid out, accelerometer routed, round outline, 8 production revisions. The NFC coil is the single hardest thing halo must reproduce and this is a licence-compatible working one.

Parametric NFC spiral generator that emits a KiCad module. halo must ship a coil GENERATOR, not a fixed coil, because the inductance is a function of the host outline (ST AN2866). Candidate to vendor and drive from ce-pcb.
KiCad-native inverted-F antenna footprints, for the bare-SoC (v2) variant of halo-core where the antenna is etched into the block itself.

column3: CHECK (vendor repo; the DW3000 Arduino lib inside is third-party)
column5: The only vendor-published DW3000 hardware repo lane C/H found. Reference for the UWB variant that re-tasks halo-core pads 9/10/11/21/22/23 as SPI+IRQ+RST.
